Before We Start

I will be assuming you are using an image that you want to have animated. For this example the image size is 720x720px and we'll have the image scroll up.

There two pieces of code needed for animation:

  1. The code for the element being manipulated div {

  2. The animation being used @keyframe [name] {

Step 1 - Creating the animation

Give @keyframe a name, for this example, we'll be using @keyframe scroll-up {

Next we'll be changing the properties of the background at specific times for the animation.

@keyframe scroll-up {

/* Beginning of the Animation */
0% {background-position: 0 0;}

/* End of the Animation */
100% {background-position: 0 -720px;}

}

We set the background position to 0px 0px at the start of the animation and have it move to 0px -720px to simulate the image moving up. If you want it to move down, then make the y value an positive. You can change how much the image moves depending on your image size. You can also use the percentage values or name values too.

Now you have completed the keyframe animation needed to have an image scroll up.

Tips:

  • If you want the image to move to the right or left, change the x value, but not the y value. Like this: 720px 0px

  • If you've scaled the image, use the size you scaled it to as the amount moved, if not, use the image's original size.

  • You can also change the other properties of the element as well.

Step 2 - Manipulating the image

For this example we'll have the background of our subverse scroll upwards, so we'll be using body.light in this example.

We'll add a bit of code to the existing code to have it use the animation you've just created.

body.light {

/*YOUR IMAGE*/
background: url( URL ADDRESS ) repeat fixed 0% 0%;

Now we just add this to it:

/*Use the animation name you've used*/
animation-name: scroll-up; 
 
/*Set a duration. The larger the value, the slower it is. This must be set or animation will not play*/
animation-duration: 5s;

/*How many times you want the animation to loop.*/
animation-iteration-count: infinite;

/*The smoothing process. Set to linear to hide looping.*/
animation-timing-function: linear;

}

And with that, your image should scroll upwards.

Tips:

  • Set the background to repeat if you want to have it scroll and not leave an absent background.

  • You can use a small image and have it repeat to fill up the entire container

  • add -webkit- -o- -moz- to your functions to enable support for different browsers.

Examples: @-webkit-keyframe [name] {

-webkit-animation-name: [name];
